subject: Request: temporary P1 coverage carve-out for KentApps (weekend latency spike)
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena@kentapps.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@kentapps.com
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected weekend P1 latency — request for temporary SLA carve-out

Hi Jasmine,

We saw several P1 incidents over the last two weekends where our user-facing endpoints had 3–6s tail latency for text-generate calls. This is outside the 500ms P1 objective in our contract and it's causing some customer-facing alerts to trip.

Investigation so far (quick summary):
- Spikes correlate with batch window alignments between 02:00–05:00 UTC.
- Our usage pattern increases due to scheduled jobs from APAC customers.
- We understand Redwood has fallbacks but the failover added extra retry latency and some requests hit Dedicated pools that were scaling cold.

We'd like to request a short-term, documented carve-out while we work through footprint changes on our side — ideally a 2-week amendment that:
- Temporarily relaxes the P1 SLA on tail latency to 2s for the weekend maintenance window (02:00–06:00 UTC), or
- Adds a contractual temporary on-call augmentation on Redwood's side covering those weekend hours (paid overtime / credit offset), and
- Agrees on an escalation path (who to call beyond normal CS hours).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can internalize an on-call augmentation for the pilot, or suggest an alternative (e.g., prioritized warm pools)? We can provide a short runbook and increase our pre-warming traffic if that helps.

Thanks,
Elena
Platform Ops Lead
KentApps

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Elena Moreno <elena@kentapps.com>, ops@kentapps.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected weekend P1 latency — request for temporary SLA carve-out

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the data points. Sorry you ran into this over the weekend.

Short answer: we can support a temporary operational carve-out for a 2-week pilot, but want to align on exact scope and on-call responsibilities before confirming. Proposed next steps from our side:

1) Rafael (CS Ops) will propose an operational plan for either: paid on-call augmentation (we staff an extra rotation) OR a prioritized warm-pool & routing override during the window.
2) Priyom (Support Manager) will outline the escalation path and P1 pager rules for the pilot.
3) We draft a 2-week SLA addendum and attach it to the HubSpot deal for signatures.

Can we aim for fast alignment so the pilot can start next Friday 4/2? If KentApps can share a short pre-warm token pattern (sample traffic) that helps reduce cold-start exposure.

I'll leave Rafael and Priyom to propose the internal plan and the attachment.

—Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, Elena Moreno <elena@kentapps.com>, ops@kentapps.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected weekend P1 latency — request for temporary SLA carve-out

Elena / team — Rafael here (CS Ops). I sketched two operational options below; both are feasible for a short pilot. I've attached a rough SLA addendum draft and an on-call worksheet for staffing math.

Option A — On-call augmentation (fastest, more predictable):
- Redwood assigns one dedicated engineer to a weekend augmentation shift covering 02:00–06:00 UTC for the pilot window.
- Response expectation: P1 acknowledgement within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 60 minutes.
- Cost: hourly augmentation rate (we can credit against next invoice); see worksheet.
- Pros: immediate human intervention, quicker decisioning for fallback routing.
- Cons: cost and rotation fatigue if extended.

Option B — Prioritized warm pools + routing override (automation-first):
- We reserve a small warm pool for KentApps traffic in the affected window and enable a routing override to prioritize your requests when tail latency exceeds threshold.
- Response expectation: automated reroute within 120s of threshold crossing, human escalation only if automated mitigation fails.
- Cost: nominal reserved capacity charge; less engineering time.

Recommended approach for pilot: Start with Option B plus a single augmented on-call for the first weekend as a safety net. That lets us tune warm pool sizing while guaranteeing rapid human fallback.

Attachment: kentapps-proposed-sla-addendum-v1.pdf (draft addendum with the 2-week pilot language)
Attachment: oncall-coverage-worksheet.xlsx (staffing / cost worksheet)

I'll be available to join the initial bridge if we kick off the pilot. If you prefer a formal PO, we can route the augmentation as a short-term addendum to your existing contract.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
From: Elena Moreno <elena@kentapps.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@kentapps.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected weekend P1 latency — request for temporary SLA carve-out

Thanks Rafael — Option B + single augmented on-call for the first weekend sounds reasonable and aligns with our internal plan to change scheduled job timings next week. A few clarifications: 

- Can you confirm the exact warm-pool size assumption you used in the worksheet? We need to ensure it covers our 99.9th percentile spike.
- For the on-call augment, who will be the primary contact and what is the phone escalation after the 15-minute ack?
- We'll need the SLA addendum attached to the HubSpot deal (KA-2027-091) for procurement sign-off.

We can start pre-warm traffic on Thursday 3/31 to help sizing. Planning note: we will also create a short runbook (2 pages) that describes request patterns and a sample pre-warm script.

—Elena
Platform Ops Lead, KentApps
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Elena Moreno <elena@kentapps.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected weekend P1 latency — request for temporary SLA carve-out

Elena — quick answers and final alignment from Support: 

- Warm-pool sizing: Rafael used a conservative +40% on your observed 99th percentile concurrency for the spike window. We will monitor telemetry and can bump in real time if needed.
- On-call contact & escalation: Primary augmented on-call: Diego (rotation alias: support-aug-1). Ack within 15 minutes via PagerDuty; if unresolved after 60 minutes, the escalation goes to Support Manager (Priyom Das) then to CS Ops Director (Marissa Cole). Phone escalation list will be included in the addendum appendix.
- HubSpot addendum: Jasmine — please attach kentapps-proposed-sla-addendum-v1.pdf to KA-2027-091 and mark the deal stage so procurement can sign.

We approve Option B + single augmented on-call for the first weekend. Pilot start: Friday 2027-04-02 00:00 UTC. End: Sunday 2027-04-18 23:59 UTC. We'll follow up with a 48-hour post-pilot summary and decide on permanent remediation.

Thanks — Priyom
Support Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
